title: Medicine through time timeline template
subject: History
source: Seeded from history/y4 lessons 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 (Medicine through time timeline template (portal printable))
intro: To understand how people in ancient times treated illness with herbs and healers

questions.q: Name a remedy from ancient Egypt that really helped.
questions.a: Honey on wounds
questions.model: Look at the Egypt slide. Honey was put on cuts. It keeps wounds clean, so it helped.

questions.q: What did Hippocrates teach doctors to do?
questions.a: Observe patients carefully and look for natural causes

questions.q: Willow bark was used for pain. What modern medicine is linked to it?
questions.a: Aspirin

questions.q: A medieval medicine jar is found. Is it a source?
questions.a: Yes: an object source
questions.model: Is it from the past? Yes. Does it tell us something? Yes, that medicines were stored in jars. So it is a source.

questions.q: Name one thing a herbal tells us.
questions.a: Which plants were used for which illnesses

questions.q: Name one thing a herbal cannot tell us.
questions.a: Whether the remedies worked

questions.q: Where did al-Razi run hospitals?
questions.a: Rayy and Baghdad
questions.model: Look at the al-Razi slide. He ran hospitals in two cities. Rayy and Baghdad.

questions.q: Which two diseases did al-Razi describe?
questions.a: Smallpox and measles

questions.q: Give one way a bimaristan was like a hospital today.
questions.a: For example: wards for different illnesses or a pharmacy

questions.q: What is the Canon of Medicine?
questions.a: Ibn Sina's large book of medical knowledge
questions.model: Read the title: The Canon of Medicine. Canon means a big book of rules. It is Ibn Sina's book of medical knowledge.

questions.q: Name one big idea in the Canon.
questions.a: For example: some diseases spread; test medicines carefully

questions.q: Into which language was it translated for Europe?
questions.a: Latin

questions.q: Put in order: test on James, notice milkmaids, result: no smallpox.
questions.a: Notice milkmaids, test on James, result: no smallpox
questions.model: First Jenner noticed something. Then he tested his idea. Then he saw the result.

questions.q: In which year did Jenner test his idea?
Where did Lady Mary Wortley Montagu see variolation?
questions.a: In Istanbul, in the Ottoman Empire

questions.q: Use the test: how many people did vaccination affect?
questions.a: Millions across the whole world
questions.model: Ask: who did it help? People in every country. So it affected millions: very significant.

questions.q: Give one reason people opposed vaccination.
questions.a: Fear of something new, or not wanting the law to force them

questions.q: Does vaccination still matter today?
questions.a: Yes: babies and adults are still vaccinated against many diseases

questions.q: Where was the Scutari hospital?
questions.a: Near Istanbul (in today's Turkey)
questions.model: Read the first slide. Scutari is near Istanbul. So the hospital was near Istanbul.

questions.q: Name two changes Nightingale made.
questions.a: For example: cleaned the wards and gave better food

questions.q: Why did she collect statistics?
questions.a: To show disease was killing soldiers and persuade the government to act

questions.q: Where was Mary Seacole born?
questions.a: Kingston, Jamaica
questions.model: Look at the first slide. She was born in Kingston. Kingston is in Jamaica.

questions.q: What was the British Hotel?
questions.a: A place near the front that gave soldiers food, rest and medicines

questions.q: Give one way Seacole and Nightingale were similar.
questions.a: Both cared for soldiers in the Crimean War

questions.q: Core: Write three facts about healers long ago (one Egyptian, one Greek, one about herbs). Use the portal response box or your book.
questions.a: For example: Egyptians wrote remedies on papyrus; Hippocrates watched patients; willow bark eased pain
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: 'Fact 1: Egyptian doctors put honey on wounds to keep them clean.'

questions.q: Extend: Why did some old remedies not work?
questions.a: They were based on wrong ideas, like charms or the four humours

questions.q: Stretch: Why was careful observation such a big step forward?
questions.a: Doctors could learn what really worked by watching what happened

questions.q: Core: Look at the source cards. For each, write what it tells us about medieval medicine.
questions.a: Herbal: plants used; monastery garden: monks grew herbs; jar: medicines were stored; tools: surgery happened
questions.model: Teacher shows card 1: 'A monastery garden plan: tells us monks grew herbs like sage to treat the sick.'

questions.q: Extend: Which source is most useful and why?
questions.a: For example: the herbal, because it names plants and illnesses

questions.q: Stretch: Why should historians use more than one source?
questions.a: To check the facts and get a fuller picture

questions.q: Core: Write a fact file on al-Razi: when, where, what he did. Use the portal response box or your book.
questions.a: About 854 to 925; Rayy and Baghdad; ran hospitals, wrote al-Hawi, described smallpox and measles
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: 'Name: Abu Bakr al-Razi. Lived: about 854 to 925. Place: Rayy and Baghdad.'

questions.q: Extend: Describe a bimaristan in two sentences.
questions.a: For example: It had wards for different illnesses. Rich and poor were cared for.

questions.q: Stretch: Why does writing down each patient's illness help medicine improve?
questions.a: Doctors can compare cases and learn which treatments work

questions.q: Core: Make a timeline of Ibn Sina's life with four dates and events.
questions.a: 980 born; about 1025 Canon finished; 1037 dies; 1100s Latin translation
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: line from 950 to 1200, mark 980 'born near Bukhara'.

questions.q: Extend: Write why the Canon was used for so long.
questions.a: It was clear, organised and full of tested knowledge, and it was translated so many could read it

questions.q: Stretch: How is Ibn Sina's idea about testing medicines like science today?
questions.a: Scientists still test medicines carefully and repeat tests to check they work

questions.q: Core: Write the steps of Jenner's experiment as a numbered list.
questions.a: 1. Noticed milkmaids rarely caught smallpox. 2. Took cowpox from a milkmaid. 3. Put it into James Phipps. 4. Later gave him smallpox material. 5. He did not get ill.
questions.model: Teacher shows step 1: 'Jenner noticed that milkmaids who had cowpox did not catch smallpox.'

questions.q: Extend: Why was vaccination safer than variolation?
questions.a: It used mild cowpox, not smallpox, so it was less dangerous

questions.q: Stretch: Would Jenner's test be allowed today? Why?
questions.a: No: testing on a child without strict safety rules and permission would not be allowed

questions.q: Core: Write a paragraph: 'Vaccination was significant because ...' Use the three tests. Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: Vaccination was significant because it saved millions, its effects lasted, and it still protects us today
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: Point: Vaccination was very significant. Evidence: smallpox was eradicated in 1980. Explain: so no one dies of smallpox today.

questions.q: Extend: Add how Muslim and English history are linked in this story.
questions.a: Variolation was seen in the Ottoman Empire and brought to England in 1721, before Jenner

questions.q: Stretch: Was vaccination more significant than the bimaristan? Give a reason.
questions.a: Any reasoned answer, for example: yes, because it ended a disease worldwide

questions.q: Core: Make a before-and-after table for the hospital at Scutari (three rows).
questions.a: Dirty wards / cleaned; poor food / good food; no clean linen / laundry organised
questions.model: Teacher shows row 1: 'Before: dirty wards. After: wards scrubbed clean.'

questions.q: Extend: Write one sentence on why she is called a pioneer.
questions.a: She was one of the first to train nurses and use statistics to improve hospitals

questions.q: Stretch: How is Nightingale's work linked to the bimaristan idea?
questions.a: Both believed in clean, organised hospitals with trained staff

questions.q: Core: Complete a comparison table: where they worked, how they got there, what they did, what they are remembered for.
questions.a: Nightingale: Scutari, sent with nurses, cleaned hospital, nursing and statistics. Seacole: near Balaclava, own money, British Hotel and battlefield care, courage
questions.model: Teacher shows row 1: 'Where: Nightingale at Scutari hospital; Seacole near Balaclava.'

questions.q: Extend: Write a paragraph answering the big question. Use the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: Yes, because she showed great courage and helped soldiers near the front, though Nightingale changed nursing for the long term

questions.q: Stretch: Why might Seacole have been forgotten for many years and remembered again later?
questions.a: Her work was less official and recorded; later historians looked again at her autobiography

questions.q: A remedy is:
questions.a: Something used to treat an illness
options: Something used to treat an illness

questions.q: Big question: if you were ill 3,000 years ago, who would help you?
questions.a: Family and healers, using herbs, honey and simple remedies

questions.q: A source is:
questions.a: Anything from the past that tells us about it
options: Anything from the past that tells us about it

questions.q: Big question: how can we find out about medicine from 700 years ago?
questions.a: By using sources: herbals, records, objects and places, and comparing them

questions.q: Al-Razi was a:
questions.a: Physician

questions.q: Big question: what made a good hospital 1,100 years ago?
questions.a: Separate wards, trained doctors, a pharmacy and care for rich and poor, as in the bimaristans

questions.q: Ibn Sina was known in Europe as:
questions.a: Avicenna

questions.q: Big question: how could one book be used by doctors for 600 years?
questions.a: It was clear and complete, and translated into Latin so European universities used it

questions.q: Vaccine comes from the Latin word for:
questions.a: Cow

questions.q: Big question: how did a disease of cows help save millions of lives?
questions.a: Cowpox gave protection against smallpox, so Jenner made the first vaccine

questions.q: Eradicate means:
questions.a: Get rid of completely

questions.q: Big question: was the end of smallpox the greatest success in the history of medicine?
questions.a: Reasoned answer using the significance tests

questions.q: Florence Nightingale was a:
questions.a: Nurse

questions.q: Big question: how can cleaning a hospital save more lives than a new medicine?
questions.a: Dirt spreads disease; cleaning stops infections, so fewer people die

questions.q: Seacole wrote about her life in an:
questions.a: Autobiography

questions.q: Big question: should Mary Seacole be remembered as much as Florence Nightingale?
questions.a: Reasoned view with evidence about each woman's work
